result.response:
I have resolved the issue where deferred fields were incorrect when following prefetches back to the "parent" object.

### Cause
When performing a nested `prefetch_related` that traverses back to a model instance of the same type as the outer model (e.g. `User -> Profile -> User`), descriptor methods (`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor`) and their `get_prefetch_queryset()` helpers were setting reverse/reciprocal cached relation values unconditionally without checking if a relation value was already cached on the target instance (`is_cached()`). Consequently, the inner prefetched object instance was being overwritten by the outer parent instance (which had a different set of deferred fields).

### Solution
In [`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-saxrj748/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L145-L655), updated `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor` (`__get__`, `__set__`, and `get_prefetch_queryset`) to check if the target object already has a cached relation before setting reciprocal/reverse relation values.
